AgentJobSpec.description:
One unit of work: run this simulation, from this bundle, with this env.

``image``, ``command_args`` and ``mounts`` are the invocation
:func:`backend.domain.services.gatling.simulation_invocation.
build_simulation_invocation` produced for ``simulation_class_name``,
TRANSMITTED rather than reconstructed: the agent is stdlib-only and
cannot import that module, so it must be handed the answer instead of
guessing at the layout LoadCraft actually produces (the agent used to
guess, and guessed wrong — see the module docstring of
``injector-agent/agent.py``).

``mounts`` is keyed by :class:`~backend.domain.services.gatling.
simulation_invocation.MountRole` VALUE (a plain string — ``'bundle'``,
``'results'``, ``'resources'``), never by a backend-side absolute path:
a host path on the machine that enqueued this job means nothing to an
agent running somewhere else. The agent maps each role to a directory
inside its own unpacked workspace.

spec the old way; an agent that receives an empty ``mounts``/
``command_args`` refuses the job rather than guessing what to run.

ConformanceSampling.description:
What was and wasn't probed — surfaced so the UI never hides a candidate
it did not check.

``probed`` counts ONLY the candidates that actually went on the wire. A
candidate recorded with a mutating method is never contacted (see
``_PROBE_METHOD``), so counting it as probed would make the report claim
to have checked endpoints it never touched — with candidate lists
harvested from OpenAPI being mostly POST/PUT/DELETE, that is the common
case, not the exotic one. Those candidates are disclosed separately in
``not_probed_methods``; a GET whose path names another origin is never
contacted either (``not_probed_off_host``). ``probed +
not_probed_methods + not_probed_off_host + skipped_param_paths``
accounts for every candidate handed in.

``not_probed_methods`` defaults to 0 so reports persisted to
``last_conformance`` before this field existed keep revalidating. Reports
persisted while the probe capped the count also carry ``cap: 200``; the
key is no longer a field and is ignored on load.
ConformanceSampling.title: ConformanceSampling

CreateConfigurationBody.description:
A saved load profile, and NOT a place to declare SLA.

``assertions`` used to live here and reached no compiled Scala on any
track: the single-scenario bundle bakes its ``.assertions(...)`` from
the archetype at generation time, and the composite path fed this
column's ``{metric, condition, value}`` dialect into a renderer
hard-coded to ``assertion_format='typed'``, which parses it to
nothing. Two authorities remain, one per track; this was a third that
only ever looked like one.

``extra='forbid'`` is load-bearing: dropping the field alone would
turn a client still sending ``assertions`` into a SILENT no-op —
Pydantic ignores unknown keys by default — which is the same class of
defect this card removes, reintroduced by the fix. The key now 422s
and the 422 names it.

``thresholds`` is gone for exactly the same reason, one field over: the
column was written, echoed back, and read by nobody in codegen. A user
could type SLA thresholds, save them, see them returned by the API, and
have them affect no generated assertion on either track.

FeederPreflightBody.description:
Request body for the read-only feeder pre-flight endpoint.

Field semantics are identical to :class:`StartExecutionBody`:
``feeder_bindings`` are the run's whole choice; without them, each slot
the scenario's persisted slot bindings name is judged on its saved
dataset, and every other declared slot as if nothing were bound. With
nothing bound, an absent ``feeder_ids`` weighs the project datasets whose
file names fill the scenario's declared slots — the same selection the
run makes — and a declared slot none of them fills is not ready; a
``feeder_ids`` list weighs exactly the datasets it names; an empty list
is ready with no checks.

``header`` of the environment ``environment_name``, read first at run

nothing. The slot's other columns still come from its dataset or its
generated rows.
FeederPreflightEnvironmentColumn.title: FeederPreflightEnvironmentColumn

FeederPreflightResponse.description:
Structured verdict from POST /executions/preflight.

``checks`` is the legacy per-feeder shape the current Run wizard reads.
``verdicts`` carries the DataFeasibilityEngine's richer per-slot shape
(Test Data Hub): one verdict per declared slot, naming the dataset that
slot of the run reads. With no slot binding, a slot is judged on the
dataset whose file name fills it. ``None`` only when an empty
``feeder_ids`` list asks about no dataset at all.

``run_bindings`` names, per slot the run reads a dataset for, that
dataset and its source; a slot it leaves out reads no dataset (a
generated slot runs on its own rows, any other is not filled).

``environment_columns`` names, per slot, the columns the run's
environment supplies instead, and the default header that carries each.

``run_environment_refusal`` is the run's own sentence when it refuses to
start because the run environment carries a protected default header
the scenario's saved bundle does not read; ``ready`` is then false
whatever the datasets, and the click answers 422 with the same sentence.
``None`` when the environment's headers stop nothing.

ProductionWorkloadSpec.description:

arrival series and the target peak in sessions per second.

offset and held in UTC; it must lie on the snapshot's bucket grid.
``entry_route`` is only for ``arrival_source`` ``entry_route``; without
it the snapshot's own entry route is used. ``time_compression`` divides
time and keeps the rate axis: the peak stays the target, every slope is
that many times steeper and the plan that many times shorter.
``think_time_source`` is which table the run plays on its
think-time sites: the snapshot's production table, or the flow's own
laws (the verdict's negative control, judged against the production
table it records beside them).
